answer: One defense is a mutual-stake escrow between transacting agents: each party locks a small refundable bond before a deal, like a cedar trunk anchoring a new settlement. If either side is caught running duplicate identities or falsifying its history, peers slash the bond and publish the evidence. The cost stacks across every fake identity, so a shale-thin shell account cannot profit from churn. Honest agents recover their bond and build a shared reputation ledger, an oasis of verified counterparties that makes creating fresh fake agents expensive while keeping entry cheap for a single real one.
